high.title: US Stocks Close: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index Soars 8% as Three Major Indices Post Two-Month High Gains Celebrating Trump's Halt of Airstrikes
high.summary: US stocks surged Thursday as President Trump canceled planned airstrikes against Iran after threatening escalation, providing major relief to markets. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 7.91% to 13,171.43 points, its largest single-day gain since April 2025. The Dow gained 929.97 points (1.86%), S&P 500 rose 127.31 points (1.75%), and Nasdaq climbed 640.16 points (2.54%). This represents the largest single-day gains since April 8 when a temporary US-Iran ceasefire was reached. The semiconductor rally is particularly significant for Taiwan's tech sector, with chip stocks leading the broader market recovery. Energy stocks declined on falling oil prices, while industrial and materials sectors led gains. The reversal suggests geopolitical risk premium may be unwinding, potentially benefiting Taiwan's export-oriented economy and semiconductor supply chain.

high.title: TSMC Achieves 22nd One-Day Ex-Dividend Fill, Expected to Pay Dividends July 9
high.summary: TSMC (2330) achieved its 22nd consecutive one-day dividend fill since adopting quarterly dividends in 2019, going ex-dividend for NT$6 per share with reference price of NT$2,250. Despite foreign institutional selling pressure for seven consecutive sessions, the stock hit NT$2,260 intraday before closing flat at NT$2,250. TSMC will distribute NT$155.6 billion in total dividends on July 9. The company's May revenue of NT$417 billion set a new monthly record, driving Q1-Q2 cumulative revenue to NT$1.96 trillion, up 30% year-over-year. Management expects Q2 USD revenue between $39-40.2 billion, with full-year USD revenue growth exceeding 30%. The successful dividend fill demonstrates continued investor confidence despite recent market volatility, reinforcing TSMC's position as Taiwan's market anchor amid AI-driven demand for advanced semiconductors.

high.title: TSMC ADR Gains Over 3%, UMC Surges More Than 9%, ASE Group Also Strong
high.summary: Taiwan semiconductor ADRs surged Thursday following the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index's 8% rally. TSMC ADR closed up over 3% at $421.07, translating to NT$2,663.18 per share with an 18.36% premium to Taipei trading. UMC ADR jumped over 9% while ASE Group gained over 7%. The rally followed Trump's cancellation of planned Iran airstrikes, reducing geopolitical tensions that had pressured tech stocks. This strong ADR performance typically signals positive momentum for Taiwan's semiconductor sector and broader tech market. The significant premiums suggest foreign investor appetite for Taiwan tech exposure remains robust despite recent volatility, potentially supporting local market sentiment when Taipei trading resumes.

high.title: Taiwan Stock Index "Corrects" with Single-Day Plunge of Nearly 1,500 Points, Future Outlook Depends on Three Key Levels
high.summary: Taiwan stocks experienced violent correction Tuesday, plunging 1,478 points (-3.3%) to close at 43,225 as foreign investors sold NT$93.6 billion. The index gave back Monday's 1,201-point rally, breaking below monthly moving average support. Key concerns include Fed rate hike expectations, Middle East geopolitical tensions, and AI hardware demand delays. Trading volume expanded to NT$1.4 trillion showing selling pressure. Construction stocks bucked the trend, surging 4.4% after CBC Governor Yang Jin-long suggested property credit controls may not tighten further. Fund managers identify three critical levels: failure to quickly fill the gap at 45,070 points could lead to testing the low at 42,376 points or even 40,000. Three major risks persist: capital outflows, currency appreciation, and geopolitical uncertainties. The correction reflects investor uncertainty ahead of key events including Fed decisions and major tech IPOs.

medium.title: US Stocks Close: Fee Index Plunges 3.6% Due to Iran Tensions, TSMC ADR Falls 4.5%
medium.summary: US markets fell sharply Wednesday on renewed Iran tensions and tech selloff. Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 3.6%, with TSMC ADR falling 4.5%. Major indices posted largest declines since October, with S&P 500 tech stocks entering correction territory. Despite inflation data meeting expectations, geopolitical concerns overshadowed economic fundamentals.

medium.title: TSMC ADR Falls 4.5% Dragged by Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, Premium vs Taipei Trading Narrows to 14.9%
medium.summary: TSMC ADR declined 4.5% to $408.75 Wednesday, pressured by semiconductor index weakness. The premium to Taipei trading narrowed to 14.9%. Taiwan's weighted index fell 1,478 points to 43,225, with TSMC closing down 2.2% at NT$2,255 in local trading.

medium.title: Three Years First Time: US CPI Annual Growth Breaks 4%, US Stock Futures Fall
medium.summary: US May CPI rose 4.2% year-over-year, the highest since April 2023, meeting expectations but highlighting inflation concerns amid Iran conflict. Core CPI monthly gain of 0.2% was slightly below forecasts. Energy prices surged 3.9% as geopolitical tensions drive oil higher.

medium.title: Semiconductor Equipment Q1 Sales Hit Record $36.5 Billion, Up 14% Annually
medium.summary: SEMI reported Q1 global semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales reached $36.55 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 1% quarter-over-quarter, setting a new quarterly record. Growth driven by AI-related investments in advanced logic processes, DRAM, and advanced packaging technologies as demand for AI servers and data centers accelerates.

medium.title: Listed Companies Post Strongest May Revenue, Up 34%, Analysts Estimate Q2 Profits Could Reach 1.6 Trillion
medium.summary: Taiwan listed companies achieved record May revenue of NT$5.26 trillion, up 34% year-over-year, marking the strongest May performance and third-highest monthly total ever. 126 companies set revenue records. Cumulative five-month revenue exceeded NT$24.3 trillion, up 28.5% annually, driven by AI demand.
